$comment: Read from Google's own discovery document: properties.runReport -> POST v1beta/{+property}:runReport, request RunReportRequest, response RunReportResponse.
title: Google Analytics report
description: Run a report against a Google Analytics 4 property.
$sideEffectsComment: `none`, and the only read-only action in the estate so far. Running the same report twice returns the same numbers and changes nothing, so a durable run may replay it freely -- which is why there is no idempotency question here at all.

request.$pathComment: {+property}, with a PLUS. RFC 6570 reserved expansion: the value is `properties/1234` and the SLASH MUST SURVIVE. Percent-encoded it becomes properties%2F1234 and Google answers 404. This is the exact opposite of Google Sheets, where a sheet named `Q1/Q2` must have its slash escaped or the request reaches a different document -- the two are one character apart in the template and both fail silently when confused.

config.label: Property
config.description: The GA4 property, written as `properties/1234567890`. The numeric id alone is not accepted.
config.$comment: The discovery document pins the shape itself: pattern ^properties/[^/]+$. So the prefix is part of the value rather than something to add here, and the default carries it to make that obvious in the UI.

config.label: Start date
config.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or a relative form Google accepts such as `28daysAgo`, `yesterday` or `today`.

config.label: End date
config.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or a relative form such as `today`.
config.$comment: dateRanges is an ARRAY of DateRange, and this connector offers exactly one range. The dotted `as` nests it -- `dateRanges.0.startDate` folds into {dateRanges: {0: ...}}, which is why the fixture and the parity suite are what prove the shape Google actually receives.

config.label: Metrics
config.description: Metric names, comma separated. For example activeUsers, sessions, screenPageViews.

send.$comment: Google asks for [{"name": "activeUsers"}], not ["activeUsers"]. A bare list of strings is refused as the wrong type, which is why `objects` exists and why the key is declared rather than guessed.

config.label: Dimensions
config.description: Dimension names, comma separated. For example date, country, pagePath. Leave empty for a single total row.

outputShape.description: One entry per combination of dimension values. Each carries dimensionValues and metricValues, in the order requested.
Total rows matching the query, which can exceed the rows returned.
The metrics in the order their values appear in each row -- the only thing that says which number is which.
